identity_label_adjudication.question: is the 1m source-identity label on 4h-barred runs a merely documented adapter limitation, or a semantic misrepresentation downstream?
identity_label_adjudication.finding_values_safe: all published OHLCV values are exact 240x1m aggregates (T4) and no reported conclusion keys on the interval label
identity_label_adjudication.finding_metadata_defect: the identity field is semantically wrong about cadence in isolation (source_identity.interval='1m' over 4h bars), and Stage4C H1 grid fields on the 4h run consequently read expected_grid_bar_count=60 / missing_grid_observation_count=59 per hour (implying expected-but-absent 1m data) instead of 'the 1m grid was never expected to be filled in 3 of every 4 hours' — a genuine misrepresentation for any future consumer that keys on these fields
identity_label_adjudication.finding_self_disclosing: the same records disclose the actual cadence (H1__observed_source_bar_count=1 per bucket, H1__coverage_status=GRID_OBSERVATIONS_MISSING) and the contract state (source_semantics=CALLER_SUPPLIED_OHLC; SOURCE_ORIGIN_UNVERIFIED; tie_order_contract=NOT_PROVEN)
identity_label_adjudication.verdict: DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION_WITH_BOUNDED_METADATA_DEFECT — NOT BLOCKED. Correctness of every reported conclusion (boundaries, completeness, placement, A/B, tests) is independently established and none consumes the defective fields. Hazard note: future consumers must NOT treat source_identity.interval as content cadence, and must NOT read missing_grid_observation_count as expected-but-absent data for non-1m feeds. Future runs should record a supplied_bar_cadence attribute alongside the contract label (documentation-level fix only; CLOSED contracts left unchanged).
